result:
**Verdict: PASS** for DG1 round 10, candidate `sha256:18fee161…c8807`. I found one new Low, non-mandatory issue (proposed **F-DG1-011**), and Node 24 could not be checked here.

**Candidate:** the recomputed candidate ID matched in the repository, in a full disposable clone at the freeze commit `265af7e`, and in the manifest. HEAD (`241a377`) is one commit later, but it only adds metadata that the candidate hash excludes (assignments, manifest, `stages.json`).

**F-DG1-131 is fixed; I verified it closed.** D-055 no longer claims the allow-lists equal real usage. It now says module code imports 4 of the 7 allowed built-ins (`crypto`, `fs`, `path`, `url`), uses none of the 4 allowed `process` members, and that the rest is reviewed headroom. My own scan of the module source gives exactly that: no built-in outside those four and no `process` use at all.

**F-DG1-130 (the `setEngine` ban) does not over-reach.** That finding belongs to code-security, so I only checked over-reach.
- The real module tree has zero violations.
- Normal `node:crypto` use stays allowed: `randomUUID`, `createHash`, `createHmac`, `randomBytes`, `timingSafeEqual`, `webcrypto` and `getHashes`.
- All 10 ways I wrote of calling `setEngine` are rejected.
- A scan of member names in the 7 allowed built-ins on Node 22.22.2 finds no other loader.
- The ban matches the name, so a module function called exactly `setEngine` would also be flagged. No module has one; noted, not raised.

**No regression.** The only product change is two test files that are excluded from the build. API contract, data model, Arabic/English text, brand tokens and the requirement register are all unchanged.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit suite | 298/298 |
| Architecture suite | 105/105 |
| My over-reach probe | 5/5 |
| Integration, two runs on fresh PostgreSQL 16 | 200/200 each, no database errors |
| Live Arabic/English stack | 108/108 |
| no-CDN, OpenAPI lint, typecheck, eslint, prettier | all clean |
| Register | all 12 DG1-final rows IMPLEMENTED with every cited file present; later-gate rows not over-claimed |

In the live run, closing a transformation by a status edit is refused with 422 and the API points to the G6 business approval. Access scoping, sign-in, paging, provisional branding and "Unknown" for missing data all behave correctly. I looked at the Arabic edit screen and the English detail screen myself: correct text direction, the Provisional badge, Unknown indicators, and "closed" is not offered. All twelve round-9 domain fixes still hold, and there are no open Critical, High or mandatory DG1 findings.

**New finding — proposed F-DG1-011 (Low, non-mandatory, documentation only, owner delivery-orchestrator).** D-055 still doesn't fully match its evidence:
- It calls the member audit "exhaustive" without saying it ran only on Node 22.22.2. The implementer's handback records Node 24, the production target, as BLOCKED, so the target was never audited. This is the same kind of gap as F-DG1-010.
- It still says the switch "prevents further adjacent-route findings", which F-DG1-130 disproved and a later sentence in the same entry contradicts.
- Its evidence column still quotes the round-9 test counts (101/101 and 294/294 instead of 105/105 and 298/298).

There is no capability or runtime impact. It could be accepted as an observation once D-055 names the Node version it ran on and records Node 24 as not yet audited.

**Not checked:** neither the lint nor the member scan ran on Node 24, because this sandbox only has Node 20–22 and no network.

The disposable clone and database clusters have been removed, and the candidate tree is unchanged. The JSON record validates against the review schema, the findings file against the findings schema, and every cited evidence file exists.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-10/`:
- `domain-reviewer.json`
- `domain-reviewer.findings.json`
- `domain-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `domain-reviewer.md`

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-10/`.
